scope: Corollary 4.10 (Terminal-witness expansion) of the manuscript “Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan” (preprints/Hard-sphere-fluctuations-on-the-regular-Boltzmann-lifespan-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e294d8e5097f8d0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In slab i, let a terminal witness be a connected true C history on n ≤ 3Λi incoming labels, of excess at most 2Γ, stopped at a contact time in that slab. It may carry arbitrary further nonnegative realizability restrictions. Sum its indicator with the full activity normalization ∑ n µn n! ∫ Fi−1,n(dZn) 1terminal witness(Zn). (4.25) For the terminal classes in Lemma 3.4(ii), this expression has the preceding retained layer expansion, with independent g inputs and initial blocks. All lower C/O components attach through particle lines to the terminal witness. The preceding variation error is smaller than every fixed power of ϵ. After the artificial-top-root normalization cost µ, the coarse part with ρ > K can also be made smaller than any assigned power by choosing K sufficiently large. The remaining low-complexity witness integrals retain their realizability restrictions.
